title: Demonstrate an understanding of agri/ecotourism as a system at micro level

lessons.title: What is agri-tourism and eco-tourism?
lessons.html:
Visitors on the farm

Tourism means people travel to visit a place and spend money there. Agri-tourism is when visitors come to a farm to see and enjoy farming. Eco-tourism is when visitors come to enjoy nature, like veld, birds, wildlife, rivers and mountains, in a way that protects nature.

Examples on South African farms

  • Fruit picking days, such as strawberries or cherries
  • Farm stalls selling jam, honey, biltong and fresh vegetables
  • Guest houses and camping sites
  • Wine tasting on a wine farm
  • Hiking trails, bird watching and mountain bike routes
  • Game drives on a game farm
  • School visits to see cows being milked

Why farms do tourism

  • It brings in extra money, especially when crops or livestock earn little.
  • It creates jobs for local people, such as guides, cooks and cleaners.
  • It helps people from towns learn about farming and nature.
  • It gives a reason to protect veld, rivers and wildlife.

Tourism as a system

A system is a set of parts that work together. A small farm tourism business has these parts:

  1. Attractions: what visitors come to see or do.
  2. Facilities: toilets, parking, rooms, a picnic area, signs.
  3. People: the owner, guides, cleaners, cooks and the visitors.
  4. Services: meals, tours, bookings, information.
  5. Natural environment: the veld, water, animals and views.

If one part fails, the whole system suffers. Dirty toilets, a rude worker or a damaged trail can spoil a visit. The visitor then tells friends not to come.

lessons.title: Your role in farm tourism
lessons.html:
Every worker meets visitors

On a farm with tourism, any worker may meet a visitor. The way you behave shows the visitor what the farm is like.

Good service

  • Greet visitors in a friendly way and smile.
  • Be neat and clean, and wear your uniform if you have one.
  • If you do not know an answer, say, "Let me find out for you," and ask your supervisor.
  • Speak clearly and politely. Many visitors may speak a different language from you.
  • Report complaints to your supervisor quickly.

Keeping visitors safe

A farm has many dangers for people who do not know it:

  • Animals such as bulls, horses and dogs
  • Machinery such as tractors and augers
  • Chemicals in stores and sprayed fields
  • Dams, rivers and steep paths
  • Snakes and bees

Keep visitors away from working areas unless a guide is with them. Never let children climb on machines or go near animals alone. Know where the first aid kit is and who to call in an emergency.

Protecting nature

Eco-tourism only works if nature stays healthy. Help by:

  • Keeping visitors on paths so plants are not trampled
  • Picking up litter and making sure bins are emptied
  • Not feeding wild animals
  • Reporting fires, damage or poaching

Working with the farm

Tourism must fit around farm work. The farm may close a trail when spraying, or move cattle away from a picnic area. Follow these plans so farming and tourism do not harm each other.

Key points

  • Agri-tourism shows visitors farming; eco-tourism shows them nature.
  • Tourism brings extra income and jobs to the farm.
  • A tourism system includes attractions, facilities, people, services and nature.
  • Friendly, clean, polite service makes visitors come back.
  • Keep visitors safe from animals, machines, chemicals and water.
